hosting.//: Order matters: later entries win where globs overlap, so the catch-all goes first and the fingerprinted assets override it.

headers.//: Every SPA route is index.html via the rewrite below, and the request path is '/charts', not '/index.html' — so the shell can only be caught by a catch-all. It must never be served stale, or a deploy stays invisible until the cache expires and the app asks for chunks the new build no longer has.
Icons and the manifest change rarely but are not fingerprinted; a day is long enough to help and short enough to fix a mistake.
Vite fingerprints everything under /assets, so a given URL's contents can never change. Firebase's default is one hour, which re-validated the whole app on every cold start.
